- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a lagged correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% per day of sentiment decay.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in early weeks (e.g., 1–5 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “sentiment-weighted bias” correction: add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment > 0.6 over last 5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–68), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until price stabilizes.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.6), model often overfits recent noise; apply a “smoothing filter” — reduce forecast by 1–3% if recent 3-day average is higher than 30-day average.
